action_summary: Round 14 named PRECISION -- a local re-run of the tests an edit touches, 'never taken', worth 16 tasks -- and this round was to build that loop. It already exists. The harness that produced the 2026-11-13 receipt gates every candidate on the tests that should start passing before it spends the whole-module run, and it stops a candidate the moment one of them fails. Recomputed from that receipt's own rows: 258 candidates pass at least one new test, 13 reach the whole-module run, 10 resolve, and ZERO candidates that passed every new test were withheld from the neighbour tests. The 245 stopped candidates in 16 tasks are each partial by construction. The breakage cost is 3 tasks of 128, not 16. Round 14's number is retracted here and locked by test. The round then asked where a candidate's content comes from at all: all 93 tasks whose issue text carries no code line get no candidate, and the generator's only content channel is the code lines in the issue text. Of the 102 stuck tasks, the issue text names every new atom for 6; against the whole project at the base commit, 15 of 26 sampled changed files need only material the project already holds; and a trace of the failing test executes the file being changed for 13 of 26 tasks and reaches the changed line for 1. The material is present; the ARRANGEMENT is what is missing, and no zero-model oracle measured here can rank arrangements.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: A benchmark receipt can contain a number nobody read off the rows. Round 14 quoted one, and it was wrong by a factor of five. The correction is not prose: it is a recomputation from the receipt's own per_task rows, and it changes what the next round should build. The lesson is the one the tree keeps paying for -- measure the artifact, not the story about it.
